Record date: 2130-01-12
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/12/30 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, productive cough with greenish sputum, and ongoing fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after a week of hospitalization for exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) complicated by pneumonia. The patient was discharged on January 8th following a course of intravenous Levofloxacin and oral Prednisone. He reports minimal improvement in respiratory symptoms, with continued severe dyspnea, particularly during exertion. The productive cough persists, with greenish sputum that remains foul-smelling. He notes that while the fever has subsided, he still experiences episodes of night sweats.
Mr. Fairfax expresses frustration with his ongoing fatigue, which has not improved since his discharge. He states that he struggles with basic activities of daily living and has not regained his appetite. He is concerned about the persistent nature of his symptoms and expresses a desire for a more definitive treatment plan.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + significant fatigue, - persistent fevers, - weight loss, + night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent productive cough with foul-smelling greenish sputum, + increased wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - + decreased appetite, - nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 130/76 mmHg - Heart Rate: 92 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 28 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 85% on supplemental oxygen (4 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in moderate respiratory distress, utilizing accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Moderate wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with rhonchi; crackles audible throughout lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with persistent bacterial pneumonia, evidenced by ongoing respiratory symptoms and hypoxemia. 2. Clinical stability noted; however, the patient remains symptomatic with significant fatigue and decreased functional capacity. 3. Persistent hypoxemia requiring continued monitoring and consideration for further intervention.
PLAN
1. Continue oral Levofloxacin 750 mg daily; reassess in 72 hours for clinical response and adjust based on culture results and sensitivities. 2. Review sputum culture results; initiate targeted antibiotic therapy if indicated. 3. Repeat chest X-ray to evaluate for any new complications, including possible effusion or worsening of pneumonia. 4. Increase supplemental oxygen to 6 L via nasal cannula; consider transitioning to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) if oxygen saturation does not improve. 5. Continue oral Prednisone at 80 mg daily to manage inflammation and assess response in 48 hours. 6. Initiate nebulized bronchodilator therapy (Albuterol) every four hours as needed to improve airflow and reduce wheezing. 7. Schedule a follow-up visit in one week or sooner if symptoms worsen; consider pulmonary rehabilitation referral to aid in recovery.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax remains under close observation with a focus on managing his COPD exacerbation and pneumonia. The treatment team will continue to monitor his respiratory status and adjust the treatment plan as needed to improve his clinical condition. The patient is advised to report any new or worsening symptoms promptly, and education regarding the importance of adherence to the prescribed therapy will be reinforced.
